items.title: CJI Surya Kant announces special bench for hearing Ladakh cases pending in Supreme Court
items.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Sunday announced that he would set up a special bench of the Supreme Court to hear cases from Ladakh pending before the top court. CJI Kant was speaking at the inaugural function of the Ladakh bench of the Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court . “I will certainly make an arrangement to set up a special bench on one day to hear all cases from the Ladakh region that are pending before the Supreme Court,” CJI Kant said. CJI Kant, however, said the cases should be argued by lawyers from Leh and Kargil. He added that advocates could appear online before the bench from the Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court's bench in Leh. “The reason is very obvious. I want that every member of the Kargil and Leh bar must feel integrated with this Supreme Court and Supreme Court bar, and you must feel that you don't represent this area alone. You are in fact representative of the bar association of India, and I can say with again assurance that your competence, your ability, and your articulation is as good as members of the Supreme Court bar. Therefore, you are not lagging behind in any manner in providing best of the assistance to us,” the CJI said. CJI Kant made the announcement while responding to Attorney General for India R Venkatramani 's suggestion that a Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court should one day sit and hold proceedings in Ladakh's calm environment, away from the "noisy scenes" witnessed in Delhi. “When I saw two courts here, I also had this feeling that I should shift the Supreme Court here only. The courtrooms are so good!,” CJI Kant said.

items.title: CJI Surya Kant inaugurates J&K High Court's Ladakh bench in Leh
items.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Sunday inaugurated Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court's newly constituted Ladakh bench in Leh. Supreme Court Justices MM Sundresh , PS Narasimha and Arun Palli , along with judges of the High Court, were also present on the occasion. Attorney General for India R Venkatramani and Ladakh Lieutenant Governor VK Saxena also attended the event. Ladakh bench inauguration - Group photo Hearing of cases at the Ladakh bench will commence from October 21. A division bench of Chief Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Sanjay Parihar is expected to take up five cases on Wednesday. Justice Parihar will also preside over a single bench and hear cases on Thursday and Friday as well. The High Court has identified a total of 75 cases for listing before the bench situated in Leh. The Union government had approved the establishment of the Ladakh bench for the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh in August this year. Following the decision, the High Court on October 5 selected Leh as the place for holding sittings of the High Court in the Union Territory of Ladakh. Before the establishment of the Ladakh bench, the High Court had two benches at Srinagar and Jammu. Ladakh bench will be part of the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, as it currently serves both Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. Ladakh was carved out as a separate Union Territory in 2019 following the reorganisation of the erstwhile State of Jammu and Kashmir. The decision to establish a bench in Ladakh is aimed at bringing High Court services closer to litigants in Ladakh, where geographical distances can make access to judicial institutions more difficult.

items.title: Jagan regrets YSRCP’s backing of 2023 Election Commissioner appointment law
items.summary: Amid protests against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister and YSR Congress Party chief YS Jagan Mohan Reddy on Sunday, October 18, said he regretted supporting a law introduced by the BJP-led Union government that changed the process for appointing Election Commissioners. Jagan made the remarks while accusing the State Election Commission of bias during nominations for local body elections in Andhra Pradesh, where political violence between the YSRCP and the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) has intensified. Jagan said that the appointments of Election Commissioners should be “neutral.” "Both the State Election Commissioners and the Chief Election Commissioners should not be nominated by the ruling parties. In the past we have supported the Union government’s mechanism to make appointments by the ruling party. But we regret it today. We regret committing that mistake. Because an examiner cannot be appointed by a student," he said. YSRCP had backed the 2023 Bill in Parliament, where the President appoints the Election Commissioners based on the recommendation of a committee chaired by the Prime Minister and comprising the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet minister nominated by the Prime Minister. Seeking reforms in the nomination process, Jagan said, "Earlier, the selection committee included the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition and the Chief Justice of India. The current arrangement gives two votes to the ruling side and one to the Opposition. The Chief Justice is no longer part of the committee. This is a flaw in the system.” Similarly, the State Election Commissioners also need to be appointed through a neutral process involving the Chief Minister, the Leader of the Opposition and, possibly, the Chief Justice of the High Court. “Such reforms are necessary to restore public confidence in elections,” he said. Speaking about the attacks against YSRCP candidates, the Leader of the Opposition said that the ruling party is creating obstacles in the nomination process by denying the candidates caste certificates, no-objection certificates and other documents. Accusing the TDP of using state machinery to win the election through unfair means, Jagan said that the police are summoning the candidates under the guise of “bind-over” proceedings and threatening to file false cases against them. items.title: Rain-battered Chennai braces for more heavy showers, CM Vijay reviews preparations
items.summary: Chennai and several other districts of Tamil Nadu are likely to receive heavy rainfall on Sunday, October 18, with the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) forecasting further intense spells amid the active northeast monsoon. The forecast follows heavy rain on Saturday, October 17, when parts of Chennai recorded more than 300 mm. The downpour inundated roads, disrupted traffic and increased the combined storage of the city’s five principal drinking water reservoirs by 237 million cubic feet (mcft) over two days. On Sunday, Chief Minister Vijay inspected the Greater Chennai Corporation headquarters at Ripon Building to review preparations for the northeast monsoon and stormwater drainage measures. The RMC has forecast heavy rainfall at isolated places in Chennai, Tiruvallur, Kancheepuram, Chengalpattu, Villupuram, Cuddalore, Salem, Krishnagiri, the Nilgiris and several other districts. The department attributed the rainfall to a cyclonic circulation over northern Tamil Nadu and adjoining southern coastal Andhra Pradesh. The RMC said significant convective cloud development over north coastal Tamil Nadu and adjoining sea areas, associated with the circulation, could bring heavy to very heavy rainfall to Chennai and its neighbourhood on October 18. The RMC has issued a yellow alert for 17 districts, particularly in northern and interior Tamil Nadu, with heavy rainfall expected to continue in several parts of the state until October 23. Isolated very heavy rainfall of up to 20.4 cm is possible in districts along the Western Ghats, including the Nilgiris and Theni, on October 20. An orange alert has also been issued for heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated places in the Nilgiris, Coimbatore, Tiruppur, Dindigul, Theni, Tenkasi, Virudhunagar, Tirunelveli and Kanniyakumari districts that day. The RMC expects rainfall intensity across Tamil Nadu to ease after October 25. Another weather system is likely to form over the Bay of Bengal around the last week of October. Meanwhile, a low-pressure area is likely to form over the southwest Arabian Sea around Monday, though it is not expected to bring significant rainfall to Tamil Nadu. items.title: Supreme Court calls internet access a fundamental right for children, rejects blanket ban
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday, October 15, held that the right to access and use the internet is a fundamental right of every individual, including children irrespective of their age. A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said the right flows from Article 21, which guarantees the right to life and personal liberty, read with Article 19(1)(a), which protects freedom of speech and expression. “We have no hesitation in saying that the right to access and use the internet is a fundamental right of every individual under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution,” the court said in its 136-page order. “Our children, irrespective of their age, enjoy the same rights, and to deny the same altogether would be as absurd as saying children below a certain age do not have a conscience worth protecting or a freedom of speech worth expressing. The safety of our children and their freedom are not at odds with each other. Our children are entitled to both,” it added. The court was considering applications filed by the NGO Just Rights for Children Alliance in proceedings arising from its September 23, 2024 judgement, which dealt with the circulation of child sexual exploitation and abuse material online. The organisation had raised concerns about continued lapses by social media intermediaries and other online platforms in complying with the earlier directions. The bench expressed disappointment at the lack of meaningful progress in tackling the circulation of such material despite its judgement two years ago. It added that recent reports placed before it had revealed “an even more unsettling reality” concerning the safety and wellbeing of children online.
